title: Range Sum of BST
statement: `root` is the root of a binary search tree: for every node, all values in its left subtree are smaller than its `val` and all values in its right subtree are larger. Add up the values of the nodes that lie between `low` and `high`, both ends included, and return that total.
constraints: The tree has between 1 and 2 * 10^4 nodes
signature: int rangeSumBST(TreeNode root, int low, int high)
notes:
## Intuition

Visiting every node and adding the ones inside `[low, high]` already works in O(n). The search-tree order lets us skip whole subtrees: if a node is below `low`, everything on its left is even smaller, so only its right side can contribute; if it is above `high`, only its left side can.

## Approach

1. Define `sum(node)`, the total of in-range values in the subtree at `node`. An empty subtree gives 0.
2. If `node.val < low`, the node and its whole left subtree are out of range: return `sum(node.right)`.
3. If `node.val > high`, the node and its whole right subtree are out of range: return `sum(node.left)`.
4. Otherwise the node counts, and both sides may still hold in-range values: return `node.val + sum(node.left) + sum(node.right)`.
5. The answer is `sum(root)`.

## Example 1, step by step

Tree `[10,5,15,3,7,null,18]`, range `[7, 15]`. At 10 the value is inside, so it counts and both children are explored. At 5 the value is below 7, so its left child 3 is skipped and only 7 is visited, which counts. At 15 the value is inside and counts; its right child 18 is above 15, and 18 has no left child, so it adds 0. Total: 10 + 7 + 15 = 32.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) in the worst case (every value in range), and less when whole subtrees are pruned.
- Space: O(h) for the recursion stack, where h is the tree height (up to n for a chain).

## Pitfalls

- Both ends of the range are included; use `<` and `>` for the pruning tests, not `<=` and `>=`.
- A node out of range on one side can still have in-range descendants on the other side; do not stop at it.
- A chain-shaped tree makes the recursion as deep as the number of nodes.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sum` | returns the in-range total of one subtree |
| `node` | the root of the subtree being summed |
| `low`, `high` | the inclusive bounds of the range |

narration.2: sum(node) returns the total of the in-range values in the subtree rooted at node.
narration.6: This value is too small, and so is everything in its left subtree.
narration.7: Only the right subtree can still hold values in range.
narration.9: This value is too large, and so is everything in its right subtree.
narration.10: Only the left subtree can still hold values in range.
narration.12: The value is in range: count it and add what both subtrees contribute.
narration.14: Start the search at the root of the tree.
